title: feat: use one upstream API per community text registration
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Requires one API and exact URL for community text models and endpoint agents; updates Zod schemas, dashboard, CLI, probes, and source docs. Responses registrations serve both public APIs; Chat registrations serve Chat only.
- Backfills existing Chat registrations only, preserving pending prices and normalizing their URLs as the previous route did. Read-only production/staging checks found no external Responses registrations. Media and managed prompt rows are unchanged.
- Fixes adversarial-review findings: trailing-slash migration routing, skipped usage-only native Chat stream billing, and the packaged CLI example. Valid streams debit once; missing/malformed usage errors without billing.
- Verified 305 targeted tests, both worker typechecks, and formatting after integrating main. Registration is separated from managed-agent PR #14360; contributor history is preserved. Addresses #14243.
- Production deployment remains separate: coordinate Enter/Gen, migration/rollback rehearsal, fresh zero-Responses preflight, and a matching CLI release. No deployment or remote database changes are included.

gist.headline: One model, one address
gist.blurb: Community text models now register with one exact upstream URL instead of a small constellation of nearly-the-same ones. The hive has put labels on the pipes, which is usually how software becomes less haunted.
gist.summary: Community text-model and endpoint-agent registrations now require one exact upstream API URL: Responses registrations can serve both public API styles, while Chat registrations serve Chat only, with existing Chat URLs backfilled and normalized.
gist.impact: Contributors get a clearer dashboard and CLI registration flow, while valid native Chat streams are billed exactly once and malformed or usage-less streams return an error without a debit.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the community model registration system as a cozy garden of labeled API pipes: one sturdy upstream pipe feeds a Chat flower, while a Responses flower branches neatly to both Chat and Responses watering cans. Polli, wearing a tiny plumber tool belt, checks that every pipe has one precise address; a friendly CRT Monitor Robot holds an exact-URL label beside a retro terminal. Small code-plants and flowers make the routing cleanup feel organized and welcoming rather than bureaucratic.
